Given data: Diameter $d = 22\text{ mm}$, Tension force $P = 75\text{ kN} = 75 \times 10^3\text{ N}$, Length $L = 200\text{ mm}$, Poisson's ratio $\nu = 0.3$, Young's modulus $E = 200\text{ GPa} = 200 \times 10^3\text{ N/mm}^2$.

Cross-sectional area of the rod:
$$A = \frac{\pi}{4} d^2 = \frac{\pi}{4} (22)^2 = 380.13\text{ mm}^2$$

**(a) Elongation of the rod ($\Delta L$):**
$$\Delta L = \frac{P L}{A E} = \frac{75 \times 10^3 \times 200}{380.13 \times 200 \times 10^3} = 0.1973\text{ mm}$$

**(b) Change in diameter ($\Delta d$):**
Axial strain $\epsilon_l = \frac{\Delta L}{L} = \frac{0.1973}{200} = 0.0009865$
Lateral strain $\epsilon_t = -\nu \cdot \epsilon_l = -0.3 \times 0.0009865 = -0.000296$
$$\Delta d = \epsilon_t \cdot d = -0.000296 \times 22 = -0.00651\text{ mm}$$
The negative sign indicates a decrease in diameter.
proTip: Always convert units to consistent systems (e.g., N and mm) before substituting values into formulae to avoid calculation errors.
